tagline: The war memorial, Hornbill Festival, and Naga tribal heartland
description: Kohima is the capital of Nagaland and the cultural heart of the state. Home to the Angami Nagas, the district sits on a ridge at 1,261m. The WWII Kohima War Memorial is one of India's most significant. The Hornbill Festival (December) draws visitors from across India.
incitetales_angle: Kohima War Memorial at dawn is among the most moving pilgrimage sites in India. Few Indians know about it.

destinations.name: Kohima
destinations.tagline: Ridge-top capital with a war memorial that changes you
destinations.description: Kohima is built on a ridge with a commanding view of the valley below. The town is the administrative and cultural heart of Nagaland. The Hornbill Festival transforms the entire town in December. Outside the festival, Kohima is quiet and walkable.
what_is_there: Kohima War Memorial — 1944 WWII site, one of India's most significant war memorials
State Museum — Naga tribal artifacts, history, textiles
Kezama Village — traditional Angami Naga settlement, 20km from town
Khonoma Village — first Indian village to declare itself a wildlife sanctuary, famous for conservation
Hornbill Festival — December, 10-day festival of Naga culture, music, dance, food
Naga Heritage Village — reconstructed traditional Naga village with museum
Ridge viewpoint — walk the ridge at dusk, view valley below
local_food: Smoked pork with bamboo shoot — the Naga standard
Naga fish curry — river fish in mustard and chili
Apong — rice beer, served in every home
Axone (fermented soybean) — pungent, addictive, quintessentially Naga
Naga green salad — boiled vegetables with chili
local_tips: War Memorial: arrive by 6am for dawn ceremony (if available), few crowds
Hornbill Festival (December): book accommodation 4 months ahead, prices triple
Khonoma village walk is best in morning — 2-hour loop through forest and fields
Kezama: ask permission before photographing people or festivals
English is widely spoken — Kohima is well-accustomed to visitors

destinations.name: Kohima War Memorial
destinations.tagline: One of WWII's most significant battle sites, now a place of pilgrimage
destinations.description: The Kohima War Cemetery commemorates the 1944 Battle of Kohima, where Japanese and British forces fought for control of this ridge. British forces held the position. Nearly 1,500 soldiers are buried here. The memorial inscription reads: 'When you go home, tell them of us and say, for your tomorrow, we gave our today.'
what_is_there: War cemetery — rows of graves, each with a name and date
Memorial stone — inscription, garden, peaceful setting
Views from the ridge — the valley stretched below
local_tips: Open sunrise to sunset — arrive early for fewer crowds
Dress respectfully — this is a place of pilgrimage and remembrance
Read the stone inscription slowly — it encapsulates the sacrifice
Spend 30 minutes minimum — sit quietly, read the names

destinations.name: Khonoma
destinations.description: Khonoma was the first village in India to declare itself a wildlife sanctuary. The Angami Nagas here have protected the forest for centuries. The village sits on a ridge with 360° views. Morning or evening walks through the village and forest are excellent.
what_is_there: Forest — protected and dense, full of birds and wildlife
Village walk — traditional stone houses, terraced fields
Viewpoint — from ridge above village, valley stretches below

stays.name: Homestays in Khonoma
stays.notes: Ask in village, family-run, meals included

local_food: Bamboo shoot curry, smoked pork, apong
local_tips: Khonoma is 20km from Kohima town — book transport ahead
Walk the forest early morning for birds — bring binoculars
Ask before photographing — locals are welcoming but appreciate consent
Stay overnight if possible — evening in the village is peaceful

destinations.name: Dzuko Valley
destinations.tagline: Alpine meadow, rhododendrons, and one of Nagaland's most beautiful valleys
destinations.description: Dzuko Valley is a high-altitude alpine meadow straddling the Nagaland-Manipur border. Accessible from Kohima, the trek is a 2-day undertaking. Rhododendrons bloom April-May. The valley floor is open, ringed by cliffs.
what_is_there: Sunrise from valley rim — 360° views on clear mornings

stays.name: Rest hut in Dzuko Valley
stays.notes: Basic, book via Forest Dept. Limited capacity.

local_tips: Trek: Kohima → Japfu base → Japfu peak (1 day hike) → Dzuko Valley (2nd day)
Guide strongly recommended — paths are unmarked
Water available at streams — carry purification tablets

permit.how_to_apply: Online at https://ilp.nagaland.gov.in or through Commissioner website
permit.notes: ILP mandatory for all Indian tourists. Apply online (as of Jan 2025). Print or have digital copy.

stops: Tezpur for breakfast (2 hours from Guwahati)
day_split.notes: Leave Guwahati by 4–5am. Direct drive via NH-27 and NH-39. Mountain road begins after Dimapur. Reach Kohima by evening.

from_dimapur.notes: Shortest route. Taxi or bus from Dimapur railway station/airport. Mountain road but well-maintained.

connectivity.mobile: Airtel, Jio, BSNL available in Kohima town. Signal good.
connectivity.internet: Available in hotels and cafes in Kohima.
connectivity.atm: Multiple ATMs in Kohima — State Bank, HDFC, ICICI

best_season.notes: October-November: clear skies, best for trekking and village walks. December: Hornbill Festival dominates — book early, prices high. April-May: Dzuko Valley rhododendrons. Monsoon: roads can be slippery.
